channel.title: E School News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from E School News (eschoolnews.com)

item.title: Teaching visual literacy as a core reading strategy in the age of AI
item.description: Many years ago, around 2010, I attended a professional development program in Houston called Literacy Through Photography, at a time when I was searching for practical ways to strengthen comprehension, discussion, and reading fluency, particularly for students who found traditional print-based tasks challenging.

item.title: Beyond the dashboard: Why K-12 educators need data literacy, not just data
item.description: Walk into any data meeting at a K-12 school today, and you'll likely see a familiar scene: educators huddled around printed reports, highlighters in hand, trying to make sense of student data spread across multiple dashboards.

item.title: On your mark, get set, print: The 3 learning advantages of 3D printing
item.description: It’s truly incredible how much new technology has made its way into the classroom. Where once teaching consisted primarily of whiteboards and textbooks, you can now find tablets, smart screens, AI assistants, and a trove of learning apps designed to foster inquiry and maximize student growth.

item.title: Measuring student global competency learning using direct peer connections
item.description: Our students are coming of age in a world that demands global competency. From economic interdependence to the accelerating effects of climate change and mass migration, students need to develop the knowledge and skills to engage and succeed in this diverse and interconnected world.

item.title: Sparking civic engagement as we approach America’s 250th
item.description: Imagine students who understand how government works and who see themselves as vital contributors to their communities. That’s what happens when students are given opportunities to play a role in their school, district, and community.

item.title: The three P’s of writing a memorable college essay
item.description: As a former admissions officer and now an independent education consultant, I’ve read thousands of college essays. The ones that earn students admission to their dream schools aren’t necessarily the most polished.

item.title: 2026 prediction: AI may unleash the most entrepreneurial generation we’ve ever seen
item.description: Picture someone sitting at a kitchen table after the kids are finally in bed, laptop open, half-drunk mug of herbal tea nearby. For years, she has had a vague idea for a business--custom curriculum design for small learning pods, for example, or a micro-studio creating bespoke art for local nonprofits.

item.title: When seconds matter: Why in-building coverage is a lifeline for school safety
item.description: During a school emergency, every minute that passes is crucial, but in those moments, a reliable connection can mean the difference between confusion and coordinated response.

item.title: AI in edtech: The 2026 efficacy imperative
item.description: AI has crossed a threshold. In 2026, it is no longer a pilot category or a differentiator you add on. It is part of the operating fabric of education, embedded in how learning experiences are created, how learners practice, how educators respond, and how outcomes are measured. That reality changes the product design standard.

item.title: The death of the static textbook: Why financial education must be “live”
item.description: Imagine trying to teach a student how to navigate the city of New York in 2026 using a map from 1950. The streets have changed names, new bridges have been built, and the traffic patterns have completely changed and are unrecognizable.
